reasons: Rule/clause mismatch: NOSOLICIT governs non-solicitation (and no-hire) of personnel, but § 12.4 is a general non-compete on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products or services. The finding's own rationale concedes that no employee non-solicit or no-hire binds Customer, which under this rule points to a compliant (or not-applicable) result, with § 12.4 properly raised under an exclusivity/non-compete rule instead.

Comment is inaccurate in substance: it faults § 12.4 for lacking a 'carve-out for general recruitment' and contradicting a 'no-hire commitment' acknowledgement, but the clause says nothing about hiring or soliciting personnel; § 12.3 already confirms Customer made no no-hire commitment, so the alleged contradiction is with the non-compete/exclusivity acknowledgement, not the no-hire one.

Fallback offered (mutual 12-month personnel non-solicit with advertising carve-outs) does not respond to what § 12.4 actually restricts, so the negotiation position is misdirected and could be read as conceding a new covenant unrelated to the deleted text.
Deterministic checks for duration and general-solicitation carve-out fail precisely because the target clause is not a non-solicit, corroborating the scope mismatch rather than a phrasing variant.
